summary.business_type: Financial Services — Forex/CFD Broker (YMYL, hybrid SaaS-product + Publisher content model)
top_findings: 100% client-side rendering sitewide: raw (non-JS) HTML contains only the <title> tag on every template tested (homepage, blog, market-analysis, regulation, legal-documents, help-center) — 0 <a href> links, 0 visible body text. Non-JS-executing AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) and any SEO tool that doesn't render JS very likely see blank pages regardless of content quality.

robots.txt disallows /fr/, /zh-Hans/, /zh-Hant/ while the sitemap lists full URL sets for all three (102 of 322 URLs, 31.7%) and every page emits HTTP Link-header hreflang pointing at those same disallowed URLs — Google cannot crawl the pages it's told via hreflang/sitemap are valid language alternates.
Sitewide soft-404: any invalid URL returns HTTP 200 with full "Oops! You're Off the Map" page content, no noindex, no canonical — creating unbounded duplicate/thin-content and crawl-budget risk.

The /en/regulation trust page names FCA/ASIC/IFSC but discloses zero license numbers or regulator-register verification links, while third-party review sites already publish more specific detail — inverting the expected trust hierarchy for a YMYL brand's own regulatory disclosure page.

Structured data and E-E-A-T quality (schema, authorship) are inconsistently applied across otherwise-identical templates: some blog/market-analysis/help-center articles have full BlogPosting/AnalysisNewsArticle/FAQPage schema and named-adjacent authorship, sibling articles on the same template ship zero schema — this pattern likely spans a large share of the 110+ article-type URLs.
quick_wins: Change the root→/en redirect hop from 307 to 301 (5-min config change)
Add explicit Allow rules for GPTBot/OAI-SearchBot/ClaudeBot/PerplexityBot to robots.txt to make the currently-implicit AI-crawler access explicit
Fix the Organization schema PostalAddress (SVG) vs sameAs Google Maps (London) location mismatch
Remove the deprecated Host: directive and clarify/remove the vague Disallow: /block rule
Generate sitemap lastmod from actual CMS updated_at timestamps instead of stamping today's date on all 322 URLs
Add a compact regulator badge + established-date trust strip above the fold on homepage and conversion pages (currently footer-only)

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Valid, well-formed XML sitemap (322 URLs, ~62KB, no dupes, no host inconsistencies)
HTTPS enforced with HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains)
Clean, descriptive, locale-prefixed URL structure with no query-string/session-ID artifacts
Correct responsive viewport meta tag sitewide
Self-referencing canonical tags present on all /en/* pages checked
Fast TTFB (135-244ms) — Cloudflare edge/origin compute is healthy

findings.title: Sitewide zero body content / zero links in raw HTML (CSR-only rendering)
findings.description: Stripping all tags/scripts from the raw HTTP response (no JS execution) across homepage, blog, market-analysis, regulation, and legal-documents pages leaves only the <title> element (47-59 chars) — no hero copy, no article body, no navigation, and 0 <a href> links found in raw homepage HTML. Content only materializes after Playwright/JS execution. No <noscript> fallback exists.
findings.recommendation: Migrate blog/market-analysis/regulation/legal/help-center templates to SSR or static generation (Next.js supports this natively) so real content and internal links exist in the initial HTML response, with client hydration layered on top.

findings.title: robots.txt / sitemap / hreflang contradiction on non-English locales
findings.description: robots.txt disallows /fr/, /zh-Hans/, /zh-Hant/ while the sitemap lists 102 URLs (31.7%) under those same paths and every page emits HTTP Link-header hreflang pointing at them. Google will exclude these from indexing ('Excluded by robots.txt') and cannot crawl them to read any on-page directive.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: either remove the three Disallow lines and let the locales be crawled, or strip their URLs from the sitemap/hreflang set and add noindex as a safety net if those markets are intentionally not ready.

findings.title: Sitewide soft-404: invalid URLs return HTTP 200
findings.description: A nonexistent URL (/en/this-page-definitely-does-not-exist-xyz123) returns HTTP 200 with a full rendered 'not found' page, no noindex, no canonical, no X-Robots-Tag. Classic Next.js catch-all route not calling notFound().
findings.recommendation: Ensure the catch-all/locale route calls Next.js notFound() so unmatched paths return a true 404/410, and add noindex as defense-in-depth.

findings.title: Missing CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options headers on a money-handling YMYL site
findings.description: No Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy headers found on any page tested. Login/account pages are exposed to clickjacking risk; MIME-sniffing is unmitigated.
findings.recommendation: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff at the CDN/app layer. Also disable the x-powered-by: Next.js header.

findings.title: Help-center template (60+ pages) has zero structured data
findings.description: /en/help-center/account-types and other article-level help-center pages ship 0 JSON-LD blocks, inconsistent with the blog template which implements BlogPosting/FAQPage.
findings.recommendation: Apply QAPage + BreadcrumbList schema to the help-center article template (see schema.md for generated JSON-LD).

findings.title: Homepage redirect chain uses a temporary 307 on the locale-establishing hop
findings.description: anzocapital.com/ -> 301 -> www.anzocapital.com/ -> 307 -> www.anzocapital.com/en. The second hop should be permanent since /en is consistently the canonical target.
findings.recommendation: Change the root -> /en redirect from 307 to 301.

findings.title: Overly aggressive cache-control on static/evergreen HTML documents
findings.description: Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate is applied identically to every page including static legal/evergreen content, and Cloudflare confirms it is NOT caching the HTML (cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC). Forces full re-fetch on every navigation.
findings.recommendation: Allow conditional GET/304 (drop no-store) for marketing/blog/legal/help-center pages, or serve with s-maxage so Cloudflare can edge-cache them.

findings.title: zh-Hans locale page missing canonical tag; inconsistent x-default hreflang handling
findings.description: The zh-Hans locale root has no rel=canonical at all. x-default hreflang is present on the homepage (pointing at the root, which itself 307-redirects) but omitted on subpages.
findings.recommendation: Add a self-referencing canonical to all locale pages; standardize x-default presence/target across all templates.

findings.title: sitemap.xml lastmod is fabricated (identical value on all 322 URLs)
findings.description: Every sitemap entry carries lastmod=2026-08-17 (today, at generation time), which trains Google to discount the field as a recrawl-priority signal.
findings.recommendation: Generate lastmod from the CMS's actual updated_at field per page.

findings.title: No IndexNow implementation
findings.description: No IndexNow key-verification file found; the site has an active publishing cadence (dated market-analysis posts) that would benefit from near-real-time Bing/Yandex notification.
findings.recommendation: Implement IndexNow given the existing sitemap and clear publish cadence.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Genuine content depth where sampled (2,898-word margin-call guide, sourced macro statistics, comparison tables, FAQ blocks) — not a thin-content site in the traditional sense
Risk disclaimers are present and reasonably thorough on regulation and article pages
Strong H2/H3 scannable structure on best-example articles (gold-vs-silver, forex-risk-management)

findings.title: No named, credentialed authorship anywhere on financial-advice content
findings.description: Blog posts credit the Organization 'Anzo Capital' as author; market-analysis posts credit a pseudonymous 'Anzo Capital - Senior Market Analyst' Person with no real name, bio, or credentials.
findings.recommendation: Add real named authors with bio/credentials and a linked author page for all blog and market-analysis content.

findings.title: /en/regulation under-discloses regulatory detail versus public record
findings.description: States broker is licensed by FCA/ASIC/IFSC with zero license numbers or verification links, while third-party review sites already publish more specific detail (FCA #739550, ASIC AFSL #362215).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite with named regulator + license number + direct register-verification link per entity; disclose which entity onboards which region.

findings.title: Bonus-focused blog post reframes a leverage-increasing bonus as a risk-safety mechanism
findings.description: /en/blog/margin-call-guide is titled 'Survival Guide: Using Your 50% Bonus as a Safety Net,' inverting the neutral risk-first framing used by every ranking competitor (SEC, FINRA, Fidelity, Vanguard) for this query.
findings.recommendation: Lead with neutral, action-first margin-call guidance before any bonus content; move promotional framing to a clearly separate section. Flag for compliance review outside SEO scope.

findings.title: Bonus/Promo content cluster (11 posts) has severe near-duplicate/cannibalizing content
findings.description: Three posts (claim-activate-50-percent-deposit-bonus, 50-percent-deposit-bonus-margin-power, 50-percent-bonus-equity-multipliers) all target the identical '50% deposit bonus' query and compete against each other in live search.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate to ~5-6 differentiated posts; 301-redirect the rest (see cluster.md for exact groupings).

findings.title: Content-operations inconsistency: best-in-class templates not consistently applied
findings.description: The strongest articles (gold-vs-silver, forex-risk-management, eur-usd-nfp market-analysis) have full schema and structure; sibling articles on identical templates (margin-call-guide, gold-forecast-ahead-of-us-cpi) ship zero structured data.
findings.recommendation: Investigate the CMS field/toggle likely causing inconsistent schema injection and backfill across the article library.

findings.title: MT4/MT5 alerts cluster (5 posts) is a smaller-scale duplicate-intent pattern
findings.description: Five posts overlap heavily on 'how to set up/fix MT4/MT5 alerts.'
findings.recommendation: Consolidate to 2-3 posts per cluster.md recommendations.

findings.title: Homepage prose is thin relative to the commercial queries its title tag targets
findings.description: 386 words of body copy, mostly UI-chrome stat callouts rather than prose, on a page whose title targets broad terms like 'forex broker'.
findings.recommendation: Expand homepage prose depth or accept that the page will only capture branded search (see sxo.md page-type mismatch finding).

findings.title: Risk disclaimers are present but consistently buried at the bottom of long articles
findings.description: Unlike regulator sources (SEC/FINRA) that lead with warning-first framing, Anzo's disclaimers appear only after promotional/educational content.
findings.recommendation: Move risk disclaimers earlier, or add a summary risk callout near the top of leveraged-trading content.

findings.title: FAQPage schema present on multiple templates — no current Google SERP benefit
findings.description: Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites on 2026-05-07. Existing FAQPage blocks are syntactically valid and pose no error risk.
findings.recommendation: Do not add new FAQPage; use QAPage for genuine single-question content going forward (e.g. help-center). No urgent removal needed.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Clean, descriptive URL slugs across all page types
Correctly self-referencing canonical tags on /en/* pages
ECN/account pages carry detailed, accurate FinancialProduct spec data (commission, leverage, margin call level)

findings.title: Homepage, account pages, and regulation page are page-type-mismatched against what Google rewards for their target queries
findings.description: SXO analysis found Google's SERPs for 'best forex broker', 'ECN account forex', and 'is Anzo Capital regulated' are dominated (75-100%) by independent third-party comparison/review content, not single-broker promotional pages. Anzo's own /regulation page does not appear in the sample of top results for its own core trust query.
findings.recommendation: For the regulation/trust query specifically, prioritize the E-E-A-T fixes above (license numbers, verification links) since self-published trust pages structurally cannot outrank independent verification sites — the goal is winning branded search and satisfying due-diligence visitors who do reach the page, not out-ranking third-party reviewers.

findings.title: ECN/account pages lack competitive differentiation (no named liquidity providers, no comparison table)
findings.description: Anzo's ECN page states '0.0 pips' as a marketing headline rather than an average with methodology, and never names a liquidity-provider tier or data-center/latency claim, unlike IC Markets and Pepperstone's equivalent pages.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'how our ECN execution works' section naming liquidity providers/infrastructure, plus a spec-comparison table vs. 2-3 named competitors.

findings.title: No above-the-fold regulatory trust badge on homepage or conversion pages
findings.description: Regulator/license badge only appears in the footer nav; the single most important trust signal for a forex broker requires scrolling to find.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact regulator badge/seal with license number into the homepage hero stat row and account/ECN page heroes.

findings.title: sitemap has no content-hub/category segmentation for 115+ blog/help-center/market-analysis posts
findings.description: All content-type URLs are flat with identical priority/changefreq per section; no cornerstone-vs-routine differentiation.
findings.recommendation: Consider a sitemap index split by content type once volume grows; ensure accurate per-post lastmod for the fast-moving market-analysis section.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: 100% JSON-LD (no Microdata/RDFa), correct https://schema.org context, absolute URLs throughout
Homepage Organization/WebSite schema is rich and mostly well-formed with 7 sameAs profiles
Blog posts (where present) and account pages carry detailed, correctly-typed FinancialProduct/BlogPosting/BreadcrumbList schema
No deprecated schema types (HowTo) used anywhere

findings.title: Zero JSON-LD on multiple sampled blog, market-analysis, and help-center article pages
findings.description: margin-call-guide, gold-forecast-ahead-of-us-cpi-20260713, and help-center/account-types all ship 0 schema blocks despite sibling pages on identical templates having full schema. Confirmed with both --mode auto and --mode always. Sitemap shows 81 blog + 28 market-analysis + 57 help-center URLs, so this likely spans a large share of content.
findings.recommendation: Investigate the CMS field/toggle causing inconsistent injection; backfill missing schema using the working sibling templates as the standard (see schema.md for generated JSON-LD examples).

findings.title: Organization PostalAddress (St. Vincent) conflicts with its own sameAs Google Maps link (London)
findings.description: Same @id node declares two geographically conflicting locations for a regulated financial entity.
findings.recommendation: Either add the London office as an explicit second location/department, or remove the mismatched Maps link if it doesn't represent the legal entity.

findings.title: Same Organization @id inconsistently typed (Organization vs Corporation) across pages
findings.description: Homepage uses Organization; regulation/about/help-center/account pages use Corporation for the same @id.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on Organization sitewide for entity consolidation.

findings.title: feesAndCommissionsSpecification populated with free text instead of required URL type
findings.description: FinancialProduct blocks on ECN/STP pages use this property incorrectly.
findings.recommendation: Point to a URL with the fee schedule, or drop in favor of the existing text-safe PropertyValue field.

findings.title: ContactPoint contactType uses non-standard value 'customer support'
findings.description: Google's recognized values include 'customer service', not 'customer support'.
findings.recommendation: Switch to 'customer service'.

findings.title: Generic untyped Thing node in market-analysis JSON-LD
findings.description: Found alongside AnalysisNewsArticle on eur-usd-nfp post; may be suppressing a more specific rich-result type.
findings.recommendation: Investigate via Rich Results Test whether this should be a specific type (e.g. FinancialProduct/MonetaryAmount).

findings.title: FAQPage used on several templates — no current SERP benefit
findings.description: Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites 2026-05-07. Markup is valid, no error risk.
findings.recommendation: Do not remove urgently; use QAPage for new Q&A content (help-center).

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: TTFB strong across all pages tested (135-244ms) — Cloudflare edge/origin compute is not a bottleneck
DOM size reasonable (~440 elements), not a CLS/INP risk factor in itself
No console errors or render diagnostics flagged

findings.title: Zero server-rendered above-fold content (LCP gated behind full JS hydration)
findings.description:
No PSI/CrUX field data available this run (no API key configured, rate-limited). Lab signals: raw HTML body is an empty hidden Suspense boundary on all pages tested — 0 , 0

pre-hydration. Render-time proxy varied 1.9s-4.2s across repeated runs on the homepage, indicating an unstable, hydration-heavy critical path.
findings.recommendation: Ship server-rendered (or static) above-fold hero content so LCP doesn't wait on full client hydration. This is the single biggest lever for LCP on this site.

findings.title: 24 distinct third-party scripts firing post-load, including duplicated tracking tags
findings.description: 2x Microsoft Clarity + Hotjar (3 session-recording tools), 2x LinkedIn Insight Tag, 5 ad-pixel platforms (Google Ads, Bing, Meta, Twitter, Reddit, AdRoll), plus an eagerly-loaded (non-deferred) crypto-js.min.js from a third-party CDN.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate Clarity and LinkedIn Insight Tag instances; lazy-load crypto-js only where needed; consolidate ad-pixel loading through GTM triggers to reduce main-thread contention (INP risk on first interaction).

findings.title: 16 first-party JS chunks required for the initial homepage route
findings.description: Review code-splitting boundaries so below-fold/modal UI isn't part of the initial chunk graph.
findings.recommendation: Audit chunk graph; defer non-critical component bundles.

findings.title: No PSI/CrUX field data obtainable this run
findings.description: No GOOGLE_API_KEY configured; local Lighthouse CLI unavailable. All CWV figures in this audit are directional lab estimates, not certified metrics.
findings.recommendation: Configure a Google API key or run Lighthouse CLI before treating any CWV number here as binding for reporting.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: robots.txt does not block AI crawlers today — /en/ is explicitly allowed under the wildcard User-agent: * rule
Content is genuinely strong for GEO once rendered: clear definitional Q&A, comparison tables, sourced statistics, SpeakableSpecification markup on some market-analysis posts
Organization schema has solid sameAs coverage including YouTube (the single strongest AI-citation-correlated platform signal)

findings.title: 100% client-side rendering with no fallback is a severe technical barrier for non-Google AI crawlers
findings.description: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot generally do not execute JavaScript at crawl scale; pre-JS HTML is title-only on every sampled page. This likely suppresses citation eligibility across the entire content library regardless of content quality — estimated platform readiness: ChatGPT/OAI-SearchBot 30/100, Perplexity 30/100, Bing Copilot 45/100, Google AI Overviews 55/100 (Google renders JS, largely mitigating the issue for Google specifically).
findings.recommendation: Same fix as the technical/performance SSR recommendation — this is the single highest-leverage fix for AI answer-engine citation eligibility.

findings.title: /en/regulation lacks the specific, extractable regulatory detail AI systems need before citing financial claims
findings.description: Uses vague, unnamed language ('esteemed financial governing bodies') with no regulator name, license number, or verification link in extractable text; its FAQPage schema covers generic account-opening questions, not the regulatory question a cautious AI system would need answered.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as direct Q&A naming each regulator, license number, and a verification reference/link.

findings.title: llms.txt returns a soft-404 (SPA not-found shell, not real content)
findings.description: HTTP 200 but not actual llms.txt-formatted content. Per policy this convention is optional and ignored by Google Search.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a real static /llms.txt listing cornerstone educational/regulatory pages.

findings.title: No explicit AI-crawler Allow/Disallow rules in robots.txt
findings.description: Everything currently falls through to the wildcard rule (which does allow /en/), but there's no way to differentiate AI-search crawlers from AI-training crawlers if the business ever wants to.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit Allow rules for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot to make the current implicit-allow posture explicit and future-proof.

findings.title: No video content despite an active YouTube channel linked in sameAs
findings.description: YouTube mentions are the single strongest AI-citation-correlated signal identified, but no VideoObject schema or embedded video was found on sampled article pages.
findings.recommendation: Embed relevant YouTube content into educational articles with proper VideoObject schema.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Images render correctly and scale properly across all breakpoints tested (no broken grids or overflow observed)
Logo/ImageObject present in Organization schema

findings.title: Image SEO was not independently audited this run (no dedicated seo-images subagent spawned)
findings.description: Alt-text coverage, file-size optimization, and WebP/AVIF adoption were not directly assessed. Score is an estimate based on visual-audit observations only (images render correctly, no broken/oversized images visually apparent).
findings.recommendation: Run /seo images against key templates (homepage, blog, market-analysis) for a full alt-text and file-optimization pass.

findings.title: Homepage hero uses busy P&L-mockup collage imagery that may read as 'get-rich-quick' marketing
findings.description: Aggressive P&L/leverage stats layered behind the H1 (e.g. '3216.52% return') is a brand-trust nuance for a YMYL site, independent of technical image SEO.
findings.recommendation: Consider toning down leverage-focused imagery in favor of more regulated-broker-appropriate visuals; flagged for brand/compliance awareness, not a technical fix.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Fix robots.txt: resolve the Disallow conflict on /fr/, /zh-Hans/, /zh-Hant/ vs sitemap + hreflang (pick crawl-and-index or strip-and-noindex)
Fix sitewide soft-404: ensure the catch-all route calls Next.js notFound() for unmatched paths
Rewrite /en/regulation with named regulator(s), license number(s), and direct verification links per entity
Add named, credentialed authorship to blog and market-analysis content (start with highest-traffic articles)
Re-frame margin-call-guide (and audit similarly-framed posts) to lead with neutral risk guidance before bonus content; flag for compliance review

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Begin SSR/SSG migration for blog, market-analysis, regulation, legal-documents, and help-center templates (architectural — engineering-owned, likely multi-sprint)
Add CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options headers sitewide
Backfill missing BlogPosting/AnalysisNewsArticle/QAPage schema on article pages currently shipping zero structured data
Deduplicate third-party scripts (2x Clarity, 2x LinkedIn Insight Tag); lazy-load crypto-js.min.js; consolidate ad-pixel loading via GTM triggers
Add above-the-fold regulator badge + trust strip to homepage and account/ECN conversion pages
Fix Organization schema PostalAddress vs sameAs Google Maps location mismatch
Consolidate the 11-post Bonus/Promo content cluster to ~5-6 posts (301 the rest)

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Build hub/pillar pages for the top 4 content clusters (Gold/Metals, Macro/Central-Bank, MT4/MT5, Bonus/Promo) with mandatory spoke-pillar internal linking
Consolidate MT4/MT5 alerts cluster (5 posts) to 2-3 posts
Add ECN/account-page competitive differentiation: named liquidity providers, comparison table vs. 2-3 named competitors
Standardize Organization @type (Organization vs Corporation) across all pages
Generate sitemap lastmod from actual CMS updated_at values instead of build-time stamping
Embed existing YouTube content into educational articles with VideoObject schema
Add a Moz API key to unlock backlink DA/PA/spam-score/referring-domain analysis (free tier, 2,500 rows/month)
Run a dedicated /seo images pass for alt-text and file-optimization coverage

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Configure a Google API key (PSI v5 + CrUX) or working Lighthouse CLI to replace lab-estimate CWV figures with certified field/lab data
Implement IndexNow given the active publishing cadence
Re-run this audit's SXO and GEO analyses after the SSR migration ships to confirm the fix resolved AI-crawler and CWV impact
Establish a content-ops check (CMS field/QA step) to prevent schema/authorship coverage from silently regressing on new articles
Capture a drift baseline (/seo drift baseline) now that this audit is complete, to track regressions on future deploys
